tested_scope: Exactly two already-durable child completion records C1 and C2 with distinct completion identities and the same canonical_child_key K; evaluate both arrival orders [C1,C2] and [C2,C1] under identity deduplication followed by canonical-key indexing with collision detection before parent aggregate construction.

probe_definition.required_guard: After completion-identity deduplication, require canonical_child_key uniqueness across distinct completion identities before constructing the ordered parent aggregate. Encountering a second distinct identity for an occupied key returns canonical_child_key_collision and constructs no parent aggregate.

observations: Order [C1,C2]: C1 occupies K; C2 is a distinct completion identity with the already-occupied key K, so reconstruction returns FAIL_CLOSED canonical_child_key_collision before aggregate construction.
Order [C2,C1]: C2 occupies K; C1 is a distinct completion identity with the already-occupied key K, so reconstruction returns FAIL_CLOSED canonical_child_key_collision before aggregate construction.
The failure classification and colliding identity set {C1,C2} are invariant to arrival order; no record is silently overwritten and arrival order cannot select the surviving child.
scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to fail-closed canonical-child-key collision handling for exactly two durable records with distinct completion identities and one shared canonical key. No claim for concurrent writers, conflicting duplicates of one completion identity, missing child keys, key normalization ambiguity, parent processed-state mutation, torn/corrupt writes, more than two children, external side effects, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one adjacent identity-deduplication failure case where two durable child completion records reuse the same completion_identity but disagree on canonical_child_key. Verify reconstruction fails closed as a conflicting duplicate identity before canonical-key indexing. Do not test concurrent writers, parent processed-state mutation, torn writes, more than two child records, external side effects, or another boundary in that invocation.
